page.title: RFP template for virtual events
page.description: A practical guide to building an RFP that covers platform needs, production scope, rehearsal plan, and follow‑up workflow for virtual events.
page.h1: What does an RFP template for virtual events cover?
page.definition: An RFP template for virtual events is a structured document that outlines platform requirements, production responsibilities, run‑of‑show details, rehearsal schedule, escalation paths, and audience follow‑up steps so buyers can compare vendors on equal terms. It also captures budget model, timeline milestones, and deliverable checklist to keep scope clear.
page.quick_answer: Start with a checklist of platform features, production roles, rehearsal dates, and post‑event reporting; then attach a budget range and timeline so vendors can respond with comparable proposals. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: Which platform capabilities should the RFP specify?

blocks.p: The RFP must list the streaming, interaction, and analytics features the event needs so vendors can confirm fit.

sections.h2: What production roles and responsibilities belong in the RFP?

blocks.p: Define each crew role, its owner, and the deliverables it produces to avoid gaps on show day.

ol: Show caller – owns run‑of‑show and cue timing
Speaker manager – coordinates rehearsals and speaker logistics
Moderator – fields audience questions and manages chat
Platform operator – controls streaming software and layout
Graphics operator – triggers lower thirds, slides, and video rolls
Backup stream engineer – monitors secondary encoder and failover

sections.h2: How should rehearsal, backup stream, and escalation be documented?

blocks.p: Create a table that maps each risk area to its timing, owner, and acceptance criteria.

head: Area
Timing
Owner
Acceptance
rows: two to five days before live
documented contact tree with decision authority

sections.h2: What timeline milestones and budget models need to be included?

blocks.p: Lay out key dates from kickoff to replay delivery and state the cost structure the buyer expects.

ul: Replay delivery within twenty four to forty eight hours
Budget model – per host licence, monthly self‑serve plan, annual enterprise contract

sections.h2: How do you structure audience follow‑up and reporting requirements?

blocks.p: Specify the data points, handoff schedule, and ownership so marketing can act on leads quickly.

faq.q: Can I reuse an existing webinar RFP for a multi‑day summit?
faq.a: A summit adds parallel tracks, hybrid venue coordination, and larger crew requirements; reuse the core sections but expand platform capacity, production staffing, and rehearsal windows to match the broader scope. Include separate budget lines for venue AV, on‑site streaming, and extended support hours.

faq.q: What budget range should I state for a moderated webinar?
faq.a: Published ranges show moderated webinars typically cost two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred per production; state a range rather than a fixed figure to allow vendors to propose tiered options. Mention any internal crew you will supply so vendors can adjust pricing.

faq.q: How do I evaluate vendor responses objectively?
faq.a: Score each response against the same weighted matrix covering platform fit, production experience, rehearsal plan, backup strategy, and reporting depth; keep the matrix in the RFP so reviewers apply identical criteria. Assign numeric weights to each category before the review begins.

faq.q: When should the replay and analytics be delivered?
faq.a: Deliver the edited recording within twenty four to forty eight hours after the live session and provide a first analytics snapshot within one week; schedule a deeper insights review at the two week mark. Include engagement heatmaps, drop‑off points, and lead qualification tags in the deeper review.
